questions.stem: The minimum energy that colliding particles must possess for a reaction to occur is called the

options.text: kinetic energy
activation energy
lattice energy
enthalpy of reaction

questions.explanation: The activation energy is the energy barrier that must be overcome before existing bonds can begin to break. Collisions carrying less than this energy simply bounce apart unchanged, which is why not every collision leads to a reaction.

distractorRationale.a: Kinetic energy is the energy a particle has because of its motion; only some particles have enough of it to react
distractorRationale.c: Lattice energy relates to the formation of an ionic solid from gaseous ions
distractorRationale.d: The enthalpy of reaction is the overall energy difference between reactants and products, not the barrier between them

questions.stem: Powdered calcium trioxocarbonate(IV) reacts faster with dilute hydrochloric acid than the same mass of large lumps because the powder has

options.text: a lower activation energy
a greater surface area exposed to the acid
more moles of carbonate
a higher temperature

questions.explanation: Breaking a solid into a powder exposes far more of its particles at the surface where the acid can reach them. More exposed particles means more collisions between H+ ions and carbonate per second, so the rate rises. The total amount of gas eventually produced is unchanged.

distractorRationale.a: Activation energy is a property of the reaction itself and is unaffected by particle size
distractorRationale.c: The same mass contains the same number of moles whether it is powdered or lumpy
distractorRationale.d: Both samples start at the same temperature

questions.stem: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction by

options.text: increasing the average kinetic energy of the particles
providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy
increasing the concentration of the reactants
increasing the amount of product formed

questions.explanation: A catalyst offers a different reaction route whose energy barrier is lower, so at any given temperature a much larger fraction of collisions carries enough energy to succeed. The catalyst itself is recovered unchanged and does not alter the final yield.

distractorRationale.a: Only heating raises the average kinetic energy; a catalyst does not supply energy
distractorRationale.c: The concentrations of the reactants are unaffected by adding a catalyst
distractorRationale.d: A catalyst changes how quickly equilibrium or completion is reached, never how much product forms

questions.stem: Raising the temperature of a reaction mixture by 10 degrees Celsius roughly doubles the rate. The main reason is that

options.text: the particles move about twice as fast
a much larger fraction of the particles now has energy exceeding the activation energy
the activation energy of the reaction is halved
the particles become larger and easier to hit

questions.explanation: A 10 degree rise increases average molecular speed by only a few percent, which alone cannot double the rate. What changes dramatically is the shape of the energy distribution: the number of molecules in the high-energy tail beyond the activation energy grows sharply, so far more collisions are effective.

distractorRationale.a: Average speed rises only slightly over a 10 degree interval, nowhere near doubling
distractorRationale.c: Activation energy is a fixed property of the reaction pathway and does not change with temperature
distractorRationale.d: Particle size is unaffected by heating

questions.stem: Excess marble chips react with 50 cm3 of dilute hydrochloric acid and the volume of gas is plotted against time. The experiment is repeated with the same mass of powdered marble and the same acid. The second curve will

options.text: be steeper at first and level off at a higher final volume
be steeper at first and level off at the same final volume
be less steep and level off at a lower final volume
be identical to the first curve

questions.explanation: Powder exposes more surface, so the initial rate is higher and the curve rises more steeply. However the acid is the limiting reactant and its amount is unchanged, so exactly the same number of moles of carbon dioxide is eventually produced and both curves plateau at the same height.

distractorRationale.a: Surface area affects only the rate; the final yield depends on the limiting reactant
distractorRationale.c: Increasing surface area speeds a reaction up rather than slowing it down
distractorRationale.d: The initial gradients differ noticeably, so the curves are not identical

questions.stem: On a graph of volume of gas produced against time, the rate of reaction at any instant is given by

options.text: the height of the curve at that point
the gradient of the curve at that point
the area under the curve up to that point
the total time taken for the reaction

questions.explanation: Rate is change in quantity divided by change in time, which is exactly what the gradient of a volume-time graph measures. A steep gradient means fast reaction, and where the curve becomes horizontal the gradient is zero and the reaction has stopped.

distractorRationale.a: The height gives the total volume produced so far, not how fast it is being produced
distractorRationale.c: The area under a volume-time graph has no useful physical meaning here
distractorRationale.d: Total time gives only an average over the whole reaction, not the rate at an instant

questions.stem: According to collision theory, the rate of a reaction is affected by the frequency of collisions between reactant particles. Which of the following factors would increase the frequency of these collisions?

options.text: Increasing the concentration of reactants
Decreasing the surface area of solid reactants
Lowering the temperature of the reaction
Using a less reactive catalyst

questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of reactants increases the number of particles per unit volume, leading to a higher frequency of collisions. This, in turn, increases the rate of reaction as more successful collisions can occur.

distractorRationale.b: Decreasing the surface area reduces the number of particles available for collisions, thus decreasing the reaction rate.
distractorRationale.c: Lowering the temperature decreases the kinetic energy of the particles, leading to fewer collisions and a slower reaction rate.
distractorRationale.d: Using a less reactive catalyst would not facilitate the reaction as effectively, potentially slowing it down.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the effect of temperature on the rate of a reaction according to the collision theory?

Lower temperatures increase the frequency of successful collisions.

Temperature has no effect on the rate of reaction.

distractorRationale.a: Higher temperatures actually increase the energy of the particles, not decrease it.
distractorRationale.b: Lower temperatures decrease the energy and frequency of successful collisions, slowing the reaction.
distractorRationale.d: Temperature does affect reaction rates significantly, contrary to this statement.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about catalysts is correct?

distractorRationale.b: Catalysts lower, not increase, the activation energy.

questions.stem: In an experiment, the rate of reaction is monitored by measuring the volume of gas produced over time. If a graph of volume against time shows a curve that levels off, what does this indicate?

distractorRationale.b: A constant rate would show a straight line, not a curve leveling off.
distractorRationale.d: The nature of the reaction (exothermic or endothermic) does not affect the shape of the graph.
